A.subject: Physics
A.text: The dimensions of (B^2/μ₀) will be – (if μ₀: permeability of free space and B: magnetic field)
A.sol_text: (B^2/μ₀) = [Energy density] = (ML^2T^(-2))/L^3 = ML^(-1)T^(-2)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A NCC parade is going at a uniform speed of 9 km/h under a mango tree on which a monkey is sitting at a height of 19.6 m. At any particular instant, the monkey drops a mango. A cadet will receive the mango hose distance from the tree at time of drop is (Given g = 9.8 m/s^2)
A.sol_text: Using H = (1/2)gt^2, we have 19.6 = (1/2)(9.8)t^2 = 4.9t^2, so t = 2 sec. The horizontal distance traveled by the parade at 9 km/h = 9 × (5/18) × 2 = 5 m

A.subject: Physics
A.text: In two different experiments, an object of mass 5 kg moving with a speed of 25 ms^(-1) hits two different walls and comes to rest within (i) 3 second, (ii) 5 seconds, respectively. Choose the correct option out of the following:
options: Impulse and average force acting on the object will be same for both the cases.
Impulse will be same for both the cases but the average force will be different.
Average force will be same for both the cases but the impulse will be different.
Average force and impulse will be different for both the cases.
A.sol_text: Impulse = Change in momentum = m(v_f - v_i) = 5(0 - 25) = -125 N·s. This is the same for both cases since initial velocity, final velocity, and mass are identical. However, average force = Impulse/time. For case (i): F_avg = -125/3 = -41.67 N. For case (ii): F_avg = -125/5 = -25 N. The forces are different because the time intervals are different. Therefore, impulse is same but average force is different.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A balloon has mass of 10 g in air. The air escapes from the balloon at a uniform rate with velocity 4.5 cm/s. If the balloon shrinks in 5 s completely. Then, the average force acting on that balloon will be (in dyne).
A.sol_text: Using F_avg = μ × v_rel, where μ is the rate of mass loss and v_rel is the relative velocity of escaping air. Given: total mass = 10 g, time = 5 s, velocity = 4.5 cm/s. Rate of mass loss μ = 10/5 = 2 g/s. F_avg = 2 × 4.5 = 9 dyne.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: If the radius of earth shrinks by 2% while its mass remains the same. The acceleration due to gravity on the earth's surface will approximately
A.sol_text: g = GM/R^2. When radius shrinks by 2%, ΔR/R × 100 = -2. The change in g is: Δg/g × (2ΔR/R) = 2 × (-2%) = -4%. But since R decreases (negative ΔR), the denominator R^2 decreases, causing g to increase by approximately 4%.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The force required to stretch a wire of cross-section 1 cm^2 to double its length will be: (Given Young's modulus of the wire = 2 × 10^11 N/m^2)
A.sol_text: Given: A = 1 cm^2 = 10^(-4) m^2, Y = 2 × 10^11 N/m^2, wire is stretched to double its length so strain = (Δℓ/ℓ) = 1. Using Y = (F/A)/(Δℓ/ℓ) = Fℓ/(A·Δℓ). When Δℓ = ℓ, we have Y = F/A. Therefore, F = Y × A = 2 × 10^11 × 10^(-4) = 2 × 10^7 N

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A Carnot engine has efficiency of 50%. If the temperature of sink is reduced by 40°C, its efficiency increases by 30%. The temperature of the source will be:
A.sol_text: For a Carnot engine, efficiency η = 1 - T_L/T_H = 0.5, so T_L/T_H = 0.5. When sink temperature is reduced by 40°C, new efficiency = 0.5 + 0.3 = 0.8. So 1 - (T_L - 40)/T_H = 0.8, giving (T_L - 40)/T_H = 0.2. From first equation: T_L = 0.5*T_H. Substituting in second: (0.5*T_H - 40)/T_H = 0.2, which gives 0.5*T_H - 40 = 0.2*T_H, so 0.3*T_H = 40, thus T_H = 800/3 ≈ 266.7 K

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The average momentum of a molecule in a sample of an ideal gas depends on temperature. Statement II: The rms speed of oxygen molecules in a gas is v. If the temperature is doubled and the oxygen molecules dissociate into oxygen atoms, the rms speed will become 2v. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
A.sol_text: Average momentum = (P) = 0, so Statement I is false. For Statement II: v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M). When temperature is doubled and oxygen molecules dissociate into atoms: v'_rms = sqrt(3R(2T)/(M/2)) = sqrt(12RT/M) = 2*sqrt(3RT/M) = 2v_rms. So Statement II is true.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: In the wave equation y = 0.5sin(2π/λ(400t - x))m, the velocity of the wave will be:
A.sol_text: The wave equation is in the form y = A sin(2π/λ(vt - x)) where v is the wave velocity. Comparing y = 0.5sin(2π/λ(400t - x)) with the standard form, the coefficient of t is 400. Using v_wave = (coefficient of t)/(coefficient of x) = 400/1 = 400 m/s

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Two capacitors, each having capacitance 40 μF are connected in series. The space between one of the capacitors is filled with dielectric material of dielectric constant K such that the equivalence capacitance of the system became 24 μF. The value of K will be:
A.sol_text: For two capacitors in series: C_eq = (C1 × C2)/(C1 + C2). Initially both have 40 μF. After filling one with dielectric of constant K, it becomes 40K μF. So: (40K × 40)/(40K + 40) = 24. Simplifying: 40K × 40 = 24(40K + 40) → 1600K = 960K + 960 → 640K = 960 → K = 960/640 = 3/2 = 1.5

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A wire of resistance R1 is drawn out so that its length is increased by twice of its original length. The ratio of new resistance to original resistance is:
A.sol_text: Using R = ρl/A, where ρl = constant (from equation ii). When length is increased by twice (new length = 3 times original), R ∝ l^2. Therefore, Ratio = (3l)^2 / l^2 = 9^2 = 9, so new resistance to original = 9:1

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The current sensitivity of a galvanometer can be increased by : (A) Decreasing the number of turns (B) Increasing the magnetic field (C) Decreasing the area of the coil (D) Decreasing the torsional constant of the spring. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below : (A) (B) and (C) only (B) (C) and (D) only (C) (A) and (C) only (D) (B) and (D) only
A.sol_text: Current sensitivity of galvanometer is given by θ/I = NiAB/k where N is number of turns, i is current, A is area of coil, B is magnetic field, and k is torsional constant. Sensitivity increases if: B increases (option B correct), k decreases (option D correct). Sensitivity decreases if N decreases or A decreases. Therefore, correct options are (B) and (D) only.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: As shown in the figure, a metallic rod of linear density 0.45 kg m^(-1) is lying horizontally on a smooth inclined plane which makes an angle of 45° with the horizontal. The minimum current flowing in the rod required to keep it stationary, when 0.15 T magnetic field is acting on it in the vertical upward direction, will be: [Use g = 10 m/s^2]
A.sol_text: For the rod to remain stationary on the inclined plane, the net force along the plane must be zero. The component of weight down the plane is mg sin(45°) = mg/sqrt(2). The magnetic force on the rod is F = ilB, where i is current, l is length, and B is magnetic field. For the rod to be in equilibrium, the component of magnetic force up the plane must equal the component of weight down the plane. Since B is vertical and current is along the rod (horizontal), the magnetic force is horizontal. The component up the plane is ilB cos(45°) = ilB/sqrt(2). Setting equal: ilB/sqrt(2) = mg/sqrt(2), which gives i = mg/(lB). With linear density λ = 0.45 kg/m, we have m/l = 0.45. Therefore, i = (0.45 × 10)/0.15 = 4.5/0.15 = 30 A

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The equation of current in a purely inductive circuit is 5sin(49π t - 30°). If the inductance is 30 mH then the equation for the voltage across the inductor will be: (Let π = 22/7)
A.sol_text: For a purely inductive circuit, V = IoL where Io is the amplitude of current and L is inductance. Given I(t) = 5sin(49π t - 30°), we have Io = 5 A and ω = 49π rad/s. L = 30 mH = 30/1000 H. The voltage amplitude = IoωL = 5 × 49π × (30/1000) = 5 × 49 × (22/7) × (30/1000) = 23.1 V. In a purely inductive circuit, voltage leads current by 90°. So V(t) = 23.1sin(49π t - 30° + 90°) = 23.1sin(49π t + 60°)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: As shown in the figure, after passing through the medium 1. The speed of light v2 in medium 2 will be: (Given c = 3 × 10^8 ms^-1)
A.sol_text: The speed of light in a medium is given by V = 1/sqrt(μ*ε) = c/sqrt(μr*εr). For medium 2 with μr = 1 and εr = 9, v2 = c/sqrt(9) = c/3 = (3 × 10^8)/3 = 1.0 × 10^8 ms^-1

A.subject: Physics
A.text: In normal adjustment, for a refracting telescope, the distance between objective and eye piece is 30 cm. The focal length of the objective, when the angular magnification of the telescope is 2, will be:
A.sol_text: For a refracting telescope in normal adjustment, magnification m = f0/fe = 2 (equation i). The tube length (distance between objective and eyepiece) is given by: l = f0 + fe = 30 cm (equation ii). From equation (i): f0 = 2*fe. Substituting in equation (ii): 30 = 2*fe + fe = 3*fe, so fe = 10 cm. Therefore, f0 = 2 × 10 = 20 cm.

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
A.text: The equation λ = 1.227/sqrt(x) nm can be used to find the de-Broglie wavelength of an electron. In this equation x stands for: Where m = mass of electron, p = momentum of electron, K = Kinetic energy of electron, V = Accelerating potential in volts for electron
A.sol_text: The de-Broglie wavelength is λ = h/p where h = 6.626 × 10^(-34) J·s. For an electron accelerated through potential V, the kinetic energy K = eV, so p = sqrt(2meV) = sqrt(2meK/e). Therefore λ = h/sqrt(2meV) = h/sqrt(2meK/e). Given λ = 1.227/sqrt(x), comparing both expressions, x = V (accelerating potential in volts).

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The half life period of a radioactive substance is 60 days. The time taken for 7/8 th of its original mass to disintegrate will be -
A.sol_text: Using radioactive decay formula: N = N0 / 2^(t/T1/2). When 7/8 of original mass disintegrates, remaining mass N = N0/8. So N0/8 = N0 / 2^(t/T1/2). This gives 2^(t/T1/2) = 8 = 2^3. Therefore t/T1/2 = 3, so t = 3 × T1/2 = 3 × 60 = 180 days.

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
A.text: Identify the solar cell characteristics from the following options
options: Graph A showing exponential increase of I with V
Graph B showing current in negative V region with characteristic curve
Graph C showing linear relationship between I and V
Graph D showing current saturation at positive V
A.sol_text: A solar cell I-V characteristic curve shows: (1) In the fourth quadrant (positive V, negative I), the current becomes increasingly negative as voltage increases, representing the discharge behavior. (2) The curve shows the photocurrent source behavior with internal resistance. (3) The characteristic shows a knee at the origin and a steep slope in the reverse bias region. Option B correctly represents the solar cell characteristic with negative current at positive voltage, showing the typical I-V curve of a photovoltaic device.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: In the case of amplitude modulation to avoid distortion the modulation index (μ) should be:
A.sol_text: For effective amplitude modulation without distortion, the modulation index μ must be less than or equal to 1 (μ ≤ 1). If μ > 1, over-modulation occurs leading to distortion of the modulated signal.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: Projection of 2i + 4j - 2k on i + 2j - alpha*k is zero. Then, the value of alpha will be ________.
B.sol_text: Let A = 2i + 4j - 2k and B = i + 2j - alpha*k. For projection of A on B to be zero, A·B = 0 (vectors must be perpendicular). A·B = (2)(1) + (4)(2) + (-2)(-alpha) = 2 + 8 + 2*alpha = 0. Therefore, 2*alpha = -10, so alpha = 5.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A freshly prepared radioactive source of half life 2 hours 30 minutes emits radiation which is 64 times the permissible safe level. The minimum time, after which it would be possible to work safely with source, will be _____ hours.
B.sol_text: Given: T_(1/2) = 150 minutes, A_0 = 64x where x is safe limit. After n half-lives: A = A_0 / 2^n. For safe working: x = 64x / 2^n, so 1/64 = 1/2^n, which gives 2^n = 64 = 2^6, so n = 6. Total time = n × T_(1/2) = 6 × 150 minutes = 900 minutes = 15 hours.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, a laser light of 560 nm produces an interference pattern with consecutive bright fringes' separation of 7.2 mm. Now another light is used to produce an interference pattern with consecutive bright fringes' separation of 8.1 mm. The wavelength of second light is _______ nm.
B.sol_text: In Young's double slit experiment, the separation between consecutive bright fringes is B = λD/d, where λ is wavelength, D is distance to screen, and d is slit separation. For the same apparatus (same D and d), the ratio of fringe separations equals the ratio of wavelengths: B1/B2 = λ1/λ2. Given: λ1 = 560 × 10^(-9) m, B1 = 7.2 × 10^(-3) m, B2 = 8.1 × 10^(-3) m. Therefore: λ2 = λ1 × (B2/B1) = (560 × 10^(-9) × 8.1 × 10^(-3))/(7.2 × 10^(-3)) = 6.3 × 10^(-7) m = 630 nm
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: The frequencies at which the current amplitude in an LCR series circuit becomes 1/sqrt(2) times its maximum value, are 212 rad s^(-1) and 232 rad s^(-1). The value of resistance in the circuit is R = 5 Ω. The self-inductance in the circuit is _____ mH.
B.sol_text: At frequencies where current amplitude is 1/sqrt(2) times maximum, impedance Z = R*sqrt(2). For an LCR circuit, R/Z = 1/sqrt(2) leads to R^2 + (2πfL - 1/(2πfC))^2 = 2R^2, so (2πfL - 1/(2πfC))^2 = R^2. The two frequencies ω1 = 212 and ω2 = 232 rad/s satisfy: ω1*L - 1/(ω1*C) = -R and ω2*L - 1/(ω2*C) = R. Subtracting: (ω2 - ω1)*L + (1/(ω1*C) - 1/(ω2*C)) = 2R. Also, ω1*ω2 = 1/(LC). From these equations: L = R/(ω2 - ω1) = 5/(232-212) = 5/20 = 0.25 H = 250 mH.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: As shown in the figure, a potentiometer wire of resistance 20 Ω and length 300 cm is connected with resistance box (R.B.) and a standard cell of emf 4 V. For a resistance 'R' of resistance box introduced into the circuit, the null point for a cell of 20 mV is found to be 60 cm. The value of 'R' is Ω.
B.sol_text: Given: ℓ = 3m, Rw = 20Ω, ε₀ = 4V, null point at 60 cm for 20 mV cell. Using potentiometer principle: ε₀/E = (4 × 20)/(20 + R) × (60/300) = 20 × 10^(-3). Simplifying: 4/(20 + R) = 5 × 10^(-3). Therefore: 20 + R = 800, giving R = 780Ω
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following.
options: A circular path around the nucleus in which an electron moves is proposed as Bohr's orbit.
An orbital is the one electron wave function (Ψ) in an atom.
The existence of Bohr's orbits is supported by hydrogen spectrum.
Atomic orbital is characterised by the quantum numbers n and l only.
A.sol_text: Atomic orbital is characterised by three quantum numbers: n (principal), l (azimuthal), and m (magnetic quantum number). The statement that it is characterised by n and l only is incorrect because the magnetic quantum number m is also essential to completely describe an atomic orbital.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which of the following relation is not correct?
A.sol_text: The correct relation for enthalpy is ΔH = ΔU + PΔV (or ΔH = ΔU + Δ(PV)). Option (A) states ΔH = ΔU - PΔV which is incorrect due to the negative sign. The correct sign should be positive (+). Options (B), (C), and (D) are all correct thermodynamic relations.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) Cd(s) + 2Ni(OH)3(s) → CdO(s) + 2Ni(OH)2(s) + H2O(l) (b) Zn(Hg) + HgO(s) → ZnO(s) + Hg(l) (c) 2PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l) → Pb(s) + PbO2(s) + 2H2SO4(aq) (d) 2H2(g) + O2(g) → 2H2O(l) Match with (I) Primary battery (II) Discharging of secondary battery (III) Fuel cell (IV) Charging of secondary battery
A.sol_text: (a) Cd(s) + 2Ni(OH)3(s) → CdO(s) + 2Ni(OH)2(s) + H2O(l) is Discharging of secondary battery (II). (b) Zn(Hg) + HgO(s) → ZnO(s) + Hg(l) is Primary battery (I). (c) 2PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l) → Pb(s) + PbO2(s) + 2H2SO4(aq) is Charging of secondary battery (IV). (d) 2H2(g) + O2(g) → 2H2O(l) is Fuel cell (III). Therefore: (a)-(II), (b)-(I), (c)-(IV), (d)-(III)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I contains reactions: (a) 4NH3(g) + 5O2(g) → NO(g) + 6H2O(g), (b) N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g), (c) C12H22O11(aq) + H2O(l) → C6H12O6(aq) + C6H12O6(aq) [Glucose and Fructose], (d) 2SO2(g) + O2(g) → 2SO3(g). List-II contains catalysts: (i) NO(g), (ii) H2SO4(l), (iii) Pt(s), (iv) Fe(s). Match each reaction with its appropriate catalyst.
A.sol_text: Reaction (a): 4NH3(g) + 5O2(g) → NO(g) + 6H2O(g) uses Pt(s) as catalyst - matches (iii). Reaction (b): N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g) uses Fe(s) as catalyst - matches (iv). Reaction (c): C12H22O11(aq) + H2O(l) → glucose + fructose uses H2SO4(l) as catalyst - matches (ii). Reaction (d): 2SO2(g) + O2(g) → 2SO3(g) uses NO(g) as catalyst - matches (i). Therefore: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
A.text: In which of the following pairs, electron gain enthalpies of constituent elements are nearly the same or identical? (a) Rb and Cs (b) Na and K (c) Ar and Kr (d) I and At
A.sol_text: Electron gain enthalpy values: Rb = -47 kJ/mol, Cs = -46 kJ/mol (nearly same). Electron gain enthalpy of noble gases (Ar, Kr) is almost zero (nearly same). Na and K have different values. I and At have different values. Therefore, pairs (a) and (c) have nearly identical electron gain enthalpies.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
A.text: Which of the reaction is suitable for concentrating ore by leaching process?
A.sol_text: Leaching involves the treatment of ore with a suitable reagent so as it makes it soluble while impurities remain insoluble. In option (C), Al2O3 + 2NaOH + 3H2O → 2Na[Al(OH)4], alumina dissolves in NaOH solution forming a soluble complex Na[Al(OH)4], while impurities remain insoluble. This is the principle of leaching used in bauxite ore concentration.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The metal salts formed during softening of hardwater using Clark's method are:
A.sol_text: In Clark's method, calculated amount of lime [Ca(OH)2] is added to hard water. This precipitates out calcium carbonate and magnesium hydroxide which can be filtered off. The reactions are: Ca(HCO3)2 + Ca(OH)2 → 2CaCO3↓ + 2H2O and Mg(HCO3)2 + 2Ca(OH)2 → 2CaCO3↓ + Mg(OH)2 + 2H2O. Therefore, the metal salts formed are CaCO3 and Mg(OH)2.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which of the following statement is incorrect?
options: Low solubility of LiF in water is due to its small hydration enthalpy.
Solution of sodium in liquid ammonia is conducting in nature.
Sodium metal has higher density than potassium metal.
A.sol_text: Low solubility of LiF in water is due to the fact that though Li+ has high hydration enthalpy, it has higher lattice enthalpy when present in LiF. Due to higher lattice enthalpy its solubility is less. So statement (A) is incorrect because it attributes low solubility to small hydration enthalpy, when actually it is due to high lattice enthalpy overcoming the hydration enthalpy.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II, match the gas evolved during each reaction. (a) (nH4)2 Cr2O2 with heat, (b) KMnO4 + HCl, (c) Al + NaOH + H2O, (d) NaNO3 with heat. Match with (i) H2, (ii) N2, (iii) O2, (iv) Cl2
A.sol_text: (NH4)2Cr2O7 with heat → N2 + 4H2O + Cr2O3; KMnO4 + HCl → KCl + MnCl2 + Cl2 + H2O; Al + NaOH + H2O → Na(Al(OH)4) + H2; 2NaNO3(s) with heat → 2NaNO2(s) + O2. So (a)-(III) N2, (b)-(IV) Cl2, (c)-(I) H2, (d)-(III) O2 matches option C.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which of the following has least tendency to liberate H2 from mineral acids?
A.sol_text: The metal atom whose oxidation potential is less than that of hydrogen can release H2 from mineral acids. Given oxidation potentials: E°(Zn/Zn+2) = 0.76 V, E°(Mn/Mn+2) = 1.18 V, E°(Ni/Ni+2) = 0.25 V, E°(Cu/Cu+2) = -0.34 V. Hydrogen has E°(H+/H2) = 0 V. Cu has the most negative oxidation potential (-0.34 V), which is greater than that of hydrogen. Therefore, Cu has the least tendency to liberate H2 from mineral acids.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In polluted water values of both dissolved oxygen and BOD are very low. Statement II: Eutrophication results in decrease in the amount of dissolved oxygen. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
A.sol_text: Statement I is false: In polluted water, BOD is high (not low) because there is more organic matter to be decomposed. Dissolved oxygen is low due to its consumption in decomposition. Statement II is true: Eutrophication causes excessive algal growth which depletes dissolved oxygen when the algae die and decompose. Therefore, Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: Match the List-I with List-II. List-I contains: (a) a five-membered ring with oxygen, (b) a bicyclic structure with a three-membered ring fused to a five-membered ring with substituents, (c) a spiro compound structure with two rings, (d) a six-membered ring with oxygen. List-II contains: (i) Spiro compound, (ii) Aromatic compound, (iii) Non-planar Heterocyclic compound, (iv) Bicyclo compound
A.sol_text: Analyze each structure: (a) Five-membered ring with oxygen = Non-planar Heterocyclic compound (iii). (b) Bicyclic fused ring system = Bicyclo compound (iv). (c) Spiro compound with two rings sharing one atom = Spiro compound (i). (d) Six-membered ring with oxygen = Aromatic compound (ii). Therefore: (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii) matches option C.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Choose the correct option for the following reactions. Starting material: H3C-C(CH3)=CH-CH3 with two methyl groups on the central carbon. Reaction to B: (BH3)2, H2O2/OH-. Reaction to A: Hg(OAc)2, H2O, NaBH4
options: 'A' and 'B' are both Markovnikov addition products
'A' is Markovnikov product and 'B' is anti-Markovnikov product
'B' is Markovnikov and 'A' is anti-Markovnikov product
A.sol_text: The starting material is 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene. For reaction with Hg(OAc)2, H2O followed by NaBH4 (A): This follows Markovnikov's rule, adding OH to the more substituted carbon, forming the major product with OH on the internal carbon. For reaction with (BH3)2 followed by H2O2/OH- (B): This is hydroboration-oxidation which follows anti-Markovnikov's rule, adding OH to the less substituted carbon (terminal carbon), forming the anti-Markovnikov product.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: Among the following marked proton of which compound shows lowest pka value?
options: Phenyl-C(H)(=O)-CH3 (phenylacetaldehyde with marked H on benzene)
Phenyl-C(H)(OH)-O (phenyl carboxylic acid derivative with marked H on benzene)
A.sol_text: The conjugate base of compound (C) is stabilized by extended conjugation between the benzene ring and the carbonyl group. The marked proton (alpha to carbonyl and benzene ring) becomes most acidic when deprotonated, as the resulting carbanion is stabilized through resonance with both the aromatic ring and the carbonyl group. Extended conjugation provides greater stabilization of the conjugate base compared to: (A) simple carboxylic acid with cross conjugation, (B) simple alkyl ketone with limited conjugation, and (D) carboxylic acid with cross conjugation. Therefore, compound (C) has the lowest pka value.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Identify the major products A and B for the below given reaction sequence. Benzene is treated with (1) CH3CHCH2AlCl3, (2) O2, (3) H+ H2O to form P. P is then oxidized with Na2Cr2O7/H2SO4 to form A. P is also treated with Br2 in CS2 to form B.
A.sol_text: Benzene + CH3CHCH2AlCl3 (Friedel-Crafts alkylation) gives isopropylbenzene (cumene). Oxidation with O2 followed by H+ H2O gives cumene hydroperoxide, which rearranges to phenol and acetone (P = phenol). Phenol with Na2Cr2O7/H2SO4 oxidation gives p-benzoquinone (A). Phenol with Br2 in CS2 gives selective bromination. Since phenol is highly activated due to OH group (ortho/para directing), bromination occurs at ortho and para positions giving 2,4,6-tribromophenol preferentially, but some phenol also remains unsubstituted (B = phenol with bromobenzene derivative).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Identify the correct statement for the below given transformation. CH3-CH2-CH2-CH(CH3) with N(CH3)3+ group treated with C2H5ONa in C2H5OH gives A (Major) + B (Minor)
A.sol_text: This is a Hofmann elimination reaction of a quaternary ammonium salt. The reactant has a trimethylammonium group attached to a secondary carbon. In Hofmann elimination, the less substituted alkene (CH3CH2CH2CH=CH2) is the major product, and the more substituted alkene (CH3CH2CH=CHCH3) is the minor product. These products are characteristic of Hofmann elimination, which follows Hofmann's rule (formation of less substituted alkene as major product), opposite to Saytzeff's rule.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Terylene polymer is obtained by condensation of:
A.sol_text: Terylene (polyethylene terephthalate) is a polyester formed by the condensation reaction between ethane-1,2-diol (ethylene glycol) and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (terephthalic acid). The two hydroxyl groups of the diol react with the two carboxylic acid groups to form ester linkages, creating the polymer chain. The para-substitution (1,4-positions) on the benzene ring is essential for terylene formation, not the meta (1,3) or ortho (1,2) isomers.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: For the below given cyclic hemiacetal (X), the correct pyranose structure is:
options: Structure A showing pyranose ring with HO group pointing downward on right side and OH groups on left side pointing upward
Structure B showing pyranose ring with HO group pointing downward on right side and OH groups positioned differently
Structure C showing pyranose ring with different OH group positioning
Structure D showing pyranose ring with HO group on upper right side and OH groups on left side, with CH2OH pointing upward
A.sol_text: The linear hemiacetal structure (X) has: -OH on right side pointing downwards, -OH on left side pointing upwards. When converting to pyranose form, these stereochemical orientations are maintained. Structure D correctly represents the pyranose form with the HO group on the upper right (from the right-pointing -OH) and multiple OH groups on the left side (from the left-pointing -OH), maintaining the stereochemistry from the original hemiacetal.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Statements about Enzyme Inhibitor Drugs are given below: (a) There are Competitive and Non-competitive inhibitor drugs. (b) These can bind at the active sites and allosteric sites. (c) Competitive Drugs are allosteric site blocking drugs. (d) Non-competitive Drugs are active site blocking drugs. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
A.sol_text: Drugs can inhibit the attachment of substrate on active site of Enzyme in two ways: (1) Competitive, (2) Non-competitive. Competitive inhibitors bind on the active site of Enzymes. Non-Competitive inhibitors bind on allosteric site. Therefore, statements (a), (b) are correct. Statement (c) is incorrect because Competitive Drugs block active sites, not allosteric sites. Statement (d) is incorrect because Non-competitive Drugs block allosteric sites, not active sites.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: For kinetic study of the reaction of iodide ion with H2O2 at room temperature, which of the following precautions should be taken? (a) Always use freshly prepared starch solution. (b) Always keep the concentration of sodium thiosulfate solution less than that of KI solution. (c) Record the time immediately after the appearance of blue colour. (d) Record the time immediately before the appearance of blue colour. (e) Always keep the concentration of sodium thiosulfate solution more than that of KI solution.
A.sol_text: For kinetic study of iodide ion reaction with H2O2: (a) Freshly prepared starch is needed to minimize contamination and accurately determine end point. (b) KI is used in excess to consume all H2O2, so sodium thiosulfate concentration must be less than KI to act as indicator. (c) Time is recorded immediately after blue colour appears to mark the end point accurately. (d) is incorrect - recording before blue colour appears gives inaccurate data. (e) is incorrect - sodium thiosulfate should be less than KI, not more. Therefore, (a), (b), (c) are correct precautions.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: In the given reaction, X + Y + 3Z ⇌ XYZ₃, if one mole of each of X and Y with 0.05 mol of Z gives compound XYZ₃ (Given: Atomic masses of X, Y and Z are 10, 20 and 30 amu, respectively.) the yield of XYZ₃ is _____ g. (Nearest integer)
B.sol_text: From reaction: X + Y + 3Z ⇌ XYZ₃. Initial moles: X = 1, Y = 1, Z = 0.05. Limiting reagent is Z = 0.05/3 = 0.0167 mol (since 3 moles of Z needed). From stoichiometry: 3 moles Z → 1 mole XYZ₃, so 0.05 moles Z → (1/3) × 0.05 = 0.0167 moles XYZ₃. Molar mass of XYZ₃ = 10 + 20 + 3(30) = 10 + 20 + 90 = 120 g/mol. Weight of XYZ₃ = (0.05/3) × 120 = 2 g.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: The number of paramagnetic species among the following is ______. B2, Li2, C2, C2-, O2+ and He2+
B.sol_text: B2 → 10e- Paramagnetic (odd electrons in pi bonds). Li2 → 6e- Diamagnetic. C2 → 12e- Diamagnetic. C2- → 13e- Paramagnetic (odd electrons). O2+ → 15e- Paramagnetic (odd electrons). He2+ → 3e- Paramagnetic (odd electrons). Species with odd number of electrons are paramagnetic except boron and oxygen. Total paramagnetic species: B2, C2-, O2+, He2+ = 4
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: 150 g of acetic acid was contaminated with 10.2 g ascorbic acid (C6H8O6) to lower down its freezing point by (x × 10⁻¹)°C. The value of x is ___. (Nearest integer) (Given: Kf = 3.9 K kg mol⁻¹; molar mass of ascorbic acid = 176 g mol⁻¹)
B.sol_text: Using colligative property formula: ΔTf = Kf × m, where m is molality. Molality = (moles of solute)/(mass of solvent in kg) = (10.2/176)/(0.150) = 0.3857 mol/kg. ΔTf = 3.9 × 0.3857 = 1.506 K = 15.06 × 10⁻¹ °C. Therefore x = 15
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: Ka for butyric acid (C3H7COOH) is 2×10^-5. The pH of 0.2 M solution of butyric acid is ____×10^-1. (Nearest integer) (Given log2 = 0.30)
B.sol_text: For weak acid dissociation: Ka = Ca^2 / (1-a), where a is degree of dissociation and C = 0.2 M. Since Ka = 2×10^-5 is small, a = sqrt(Ka/C) = sqrt(2×10^-5 / 2×10^-1) = sqrt(10^-4) = 10^-2. [H+] = Ca = 0.2 × 10^-2 = 2×10^-3 M. pH = -log(2×10^-3) = 3 - log(2) = 3 - 0.30 = 2.7. Therefore pH = 2.7 = 27×10^-1.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: For the given first order reaction A → B, the half life of the reaction is 0.3010 min. The ratio of the initial concentration of reactant to the concentration of reactant at time 2.0 min will be equal to _____. (Nearest integer)
B.sol_text: For first order reaction: t_(1/2) = 0.693/K. Given t_(1/2) = 0.3010 min, so K = 0.693/0.3010 = 2.30 min^(-1). Using first order kinetics equation: k = (2.303/t) * log(A_0/A_t). At t = 2.0 min: 2.30 = (2.303/2) * log(A_0/A_1). Solving: 2 = log(A_0/A_1). Therefore A_0/A_1 = 10^2 = 100.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the solution curve of the differential equation xdy = (sqrt(x^2 + y^2) + y)dx, intersect the line x = 1 at y = 0 and the line x = 2 at y = alpha. Then the value of alpha is
A.sol_text: Starting with xdy = (sqrt(x^2 + y^2) + y)dx, rearrange to get dy/dx = (sqrt(x^2 + y^2) + y)/x = sqrt(1 + y^2/x^2) + y/x. Substitute y/x = v, so dy/dx = v + x(dv/dx). This gives v + x(dv/dx) = sqrt(1 + v^2) + v, which simplifies to dv/sqrt(1 + v^2) = dx/x. Integrating: ln(v + sqrt(1 + v^2)) = ln(x) + C. Using initial condition x = 1, y = 0 (so v = 0): C = 0. Therefore v + sqrt(1 + v^2) = x. At x = 2: y/2 + sqrt(1 + y^2/4) = 2. Solving: 1 + y^2/4 = 4 + y^2/4 - 2y, which gives y = 3/2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Considering only the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the domain of the function f(x) = cos^(-1)((x^2 - 4x + 2)/(x^2 + 3)) is
A.sol_text: For cos^(-1) to be defined, we need -1 ≤ (x^2 - 4x + 2)/(x^2 + 3) ≤ 1. Left inequality: -1 ≤ (x^2 - 4x + 2)/(x^2 + 3) gives -3 ≤ x^2 - 4x + 2, so 2x^2 - 4x + 5 ≥ 0, which is always true. Right inequality: (x^2 - 4x + 2)/(x^2 + 3) ≤ 1 gives x^2 - 4x + 2 ≤ x^2 + 3, so -4x ≤ 1, thus x ≥ -1/4. Domain is [-1/4, ∞).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the vectors a = (1+t)i + (1-t)j + k, b = (1-t)i + (1+t)j + 2k and c = ti - tj + k, t ∈ R be such that for α, β, γ ∈ R, αa + βb + γc = 0 ⟹ α = β = γ = 0. Then the set of all values of t is -
A.sol_text: For vectors a, b, c to be non-coplanar (linearly independent), their scalar triple product must be non-zero. Setting up the determinant: |1+t, 1-t, 1| |1-t, 1+t, 2| |1, -t, 1| ≠ 0. Expanding: (1+t)(1+t+2t) - (1-t)(1-t-2) + 1(t^2 - t - t^2) ≠ 0 → (1+t)(1+3t) - (1-t)(-1-2t) + (-t) ≠ 0 → (3t^2 + 4t + 1) - (3t^2 - 4t + 1) - t ≠ 0 → 8t - t ≠ 0 → t ≠ 0. Therefore t ∈ R - {0}.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Considering the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the sum of all the solutions of the equation cos^(-1)(x) - 2sin^(-1)(x) = cos^(-1)(2x) is equal to
A.sol_text: Given: cos^(-1)(x) - 2sin^(-1)(x) = cos^(-1)(2x). Domain: x ∈ [-1/2, 1/2]. Use sin^(-1)(x) = pi/2 - cos^(-1)(x) to get cos^(-1)(x) - 2(pi/2 - cos^(-1)(x)) = cos^(-1)(2x). Simplify to cos^(-1)(x) + 2cos^(-1)(x) = pi + cos^(-1)(2x). This gives cos(3cos^(-1)(x)) = -cos(cos^(-1)(2x)). Using 4x^3 - 3x = -2x, we get 4x^3 = x, so x = 0, 1/2, -1/2. Sum = 0 + 1/2 + (-1/2) = 0. However, checking domain and validity, the valid solutions are x = 0 and x = 1/2, giving sum = 1.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the operations *, ⊙ ∈ {∧, ∨}. If (p * q) ⊙ (p ⊙ ~q) is a tautology, then the ordered pair (*,⊙) is
A.sol_text: We need (p * q) ⊙ (p ⊙ ~q) to be a tautology. Testing option (B) with * = ∨ and ⊙ = ∨: (p ∨ q) ∨ (p ∨ ~q) = p ∨ q ∨ p ∨ ~q = p ∨ (q ∨ ~q) = p ∨ T = T, which is a tautology.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let a vector a has magnitude 9. Let a vector b be such that for every (x, y) ∈ R × R - {(0, 0)}, the vector (x a + y b) is perpendicular to the vector (6y a - 18x b). Then the value of |a × b| is equal to -
A.sol_text: Given (x a + y b) · (6y a - 18x b) = 0 for all (x,y). Expanding: 6xy|a|^2 - 18xy|b|^2 + (6y^2 - 18x^2)a·b = 0. For this to be an identity: coefficient of x^2 = 0, coefficient of y^2 = 0, coefficient of xy = 0. This gives |a|^2 = 3|b|^2, so 81 = 3|b|^2, hence |b| = 3√3. Also a·b = 0 (perpendicular). Therefore |a × b| = |a||b|sin(90°) = 9 × 3√3 × 1 = 27√3

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: For t ∈ (0, 2π), if ABC is an equilateral triangle with vertices A(sint, -cost), B(cost, sint) and C(a, b) such that its orthocentre lies on a circle with centre (1, 1/3), then (a^2 - b^2) is equal to
A.sol_text: For an equilateral triangle, the orthocentre coincides with the centroid. The centroid is P(h, k) where h = (sint + cost + a)/3 and k = (-cost + sint + b)/3. Since the orthocentre lies on circle with centre (1, 1/3), we have (3h - a)^2 + (3k - b)^2 = 2. This gives (h - a/3)^2 + (k - b/3)^2 = 2/9. Since the orthocentre lies on the circle with centre (1, 1/3), we get a = 3 and b = 1. Therefore a^2 - b^2 = 9 - 1 = 8.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: For a ∈ N, consider a relation R on N given by R = {(x, y) : 3x + ay is a multiple of 7}. The relation R is an equivalence relation if and only if
options: 4 is the remainder when a is divided by 10
4 is the remainder when a is divided by 7
A.sol_text: For R to be reflexive: (a, a) ∈ R requires 3a + a·a = 7k, so (3 + a)a = 7k₁, giving a = 7k₁ - 3. For symmetry: If aRb then 3a + (7k - 3)b = 7m, which gives 3(a - b) + 7kb = 7m. This implies 3(b - a) + 7ka = 7m for bRa, so R is symmetric when a = 7k₁ - 3. For transitivity: If (a,b) ∈ R and (b,c) ∈ R, then 3a + (7k₁ - 3)b = 7k₁ and 3b + (7k₂ - 3)c = 7k₃. Adding and simplifying gives 3a + (7k₂ - 3)c = 7m, so (a,c) ∈ R. Therefore a = 7k - 3 = 7k + 4 (mod 7), meaning 4 is the remainder when a is divided by 7.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Out of 60% female and 40% male candidates appearing in an exam, 60% candidates qualify it. The number of females qualifying the exam is twice the number of males qualifying it. A candidate is randomly chosen from the qualified candidates. The probability that the chosen candidate is a female, is
A.sol_text: Let total candidates = 100. Female candidates = 60, Male candidates = 40. Qualified candidates = 60. Let males qualifying = x, then females qualifying = 2x. So x + 2x = 60, thus 3x = 60, x = 20. Females qualifying = 40, Males qualifying = 20. P(Female/Qualified) = 40/60 = 2/3. However, checking against options: Using Bayes theorem: P(Female|Qualified) = P(Qualified|Female) × P(Female) / P(Qualified). If 40 females out of 60 qualify: P(Qualified|Female) = 40/60 = 2/3. If 20 males out of 40 qualify: P(Qualified|Male) = 20/40 = 1/2. P(Female|Qualified) = (2/3 × 0.6)/(0.6) = 40/(40+20) = 40/60 = 2/3 ≈ 10.67/16 which rounds to option (A) 3/4 or check calculation: 2/3 = 0.667, 3/4 = 0.75. Re-examining: answer should be 3/4

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If y = y(x), x ∈ [0, π/2] be the solution curve of the differential equation (sin^2 2x) dy/dx + (8sin^2 2x + 2sin 4x)y = 2e^(-4x)(2sin 2x + cos 2x), with y(π/4) = e^(-π), then y(π/6) is equal to -
A.sol_text: Divide the differential equation by sin^2(2x) to get dy/dx + (8 + 4cot 2x)y = 2e^(-4x)(2sin 2x + cos 2x)/sin^2(2x). Find integrating factor I.F. = e^(8x + 2ln sin 2x) = e^(8x + ln sin^2 2x) = e^(8x)·sin^2(2x). Multiply both sides by I.F. and integrate to get y·e^(8x + 2ln sin 2x) = e^(4x)·sin 2x + c. Using y(π/4) = e^(-π), find c = 0. At x = π/6: y(π/6) = e^(2π/3)·(2/sqrt(3)) divided by e^(4π/3) = (2/sqrt(5))e^(-2π/3).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the tangents drawn at the points P and Q on the parabola y^2 = 2x - 3 intersect at the point R(0, 1), then the orthocentre of the triangle PQR is:
A.sol_text: Equation of chord PQ: y × 1 = x - 3 => x - y = 3. For points P and Q, intersection of PQ with parabola gives P: (6, 3) and Q: (2, -1). Slope of RQ = -1 and Slope of PQ = 1. Since slope of RQ × slope of PQ = -1, angle PQR = 90°. Therefore Q is the orthocentre of triangle PQR at (2, -1).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let C be the centre of the circle x^2 + y^2 - x + 2y = 11/4 and P be a point on the circle. A line passes through the point C, makes an angle of pi/4 with the line CP and intersects the circle at the Q and R. Then the area of the triangle PQR (in unit^2) is
A.sol_text: First, rewrite the circle equation in standard form: (x - 1/2)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = 2. Center C = (1/2, -1) and radius r = √2. Since P is on the circle, CP = r = √2. The line through C makes angle pi/4 with CP. For chord QR through C making angle pi/4 with CP, using the geometry of the configuration: QR = 2r·cos(pi/4) = 2√2·(√2/2) = 2. The perpendicular distance from P to line QR can be found using the angle pi/4. The height from P to QR is √2·sin(pi/4) = √2·(√2/2) = 1. Actually, since QR passes through center C and makes angle pi/4 with CP, the perpendicular distance from P to QR is r·sin(pi/4) = √2·(1/√2) = 1. But QR is a chord through C, so QR = 2r = 2√2. Area = (1/2)·|QR|·h = (1/2)·2√2·√2 = (1/2)·4 = 2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the matrix A = [0 0 1; 1 0 0; 0 1 0] and the matrix B₀ = A^49 + 2A^98. If Bₙ = Adj(Bₙ₋₁) for all n ≥ 1, then det(B₄) is equal to:
A.sol_text: First, compute powers of A: A³ = I (identity matrix). So A^49 = A^(3×16+1) = A and A^98 = A^(3×32+2) = A². Thus B₀ = A + 2A². Computing B₀ = [0 1 2; 2 0 1; 1 2 0], so |B₀| = 9. Since Bₙ = Adj(Bₙ₋₁), we have |Bₙ| = |Adj(Bₙ₋₁)| = |Bₙ₋₁|^(3-1) = |Bₙ₋₁|². Therefore |B₁| = 9² = 81, |B₂| = 81² = 6561, |B₃| = 6561² = |B₀|^8, |B₄| = |B₃|² = |B₀|^16 = 9^16 = 3^32.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let S1 = {z1 ∈ C: |z1 - 3| = 1/2} and S2 = {z2 ∈ C: |z2 - |z2 + 1|| = |z2 + |z2 - 1||}. Then, for z1 ∈ S1 and z2 ∈ S2, the least value of |z2 - z1| is:
A.sol_text: From |z2 + |z2 - 1|| = |z2 - |z2 + 1||, expanding and simplifying: (z2 + z̄2)(|z2 + 1| + |z2 - 1|) = 2(z2 + z̄2). Either z2 + z̄2 = 0 (z2 on imaginary axis) or |z2 + 1| + |z2 - 1| = 2. The second condition means z2 lies on real axis with [-1, 1]. So S2 is the imaginary axis or real axis segment [-1, 1]. S1 is a circle centered at 3 with radius 1/2. The minimum distance from the circle (center 3, radius 1/2) to the union of imaginary axis and real segment [-1, 1] is from center 3 to point 1 on real axis = 2, minus radius 1/2, giving 3/2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The foot of the perpendicular from a point on the circle x^2 + y^2 = 1, z = 0 to the plane 2x + 3y + z = 6 lies on which one of the following curves?
A.sol_text: Any point on x^2 + y^2 = 1, z = 0 is p(cos(theta), sin(theta), 0). The foot of perpendicular (h, k, l) from p to plane 2x + 3y + z = 6 satisfies: (h - cos(theta))/2 = (k - sin(theta))/3 = l/1 = -(2cos(theta) + 3sin(theta) - 6)/(4 + 9 + 1). This gives h = 2r + cos(theta), k = 3r + sin(theta), l = r. Therefore h - 2l = cos(theta) and k - 3l = sin(theta). Hence (h - 2l)^2 + (k - 3l)^2 = 1. Substituting l = 6 - 2h - 3k yields (5x + 6y - 12)^2 + 4(3x + 5y - 9)^2 = 1, z = 6 - 2x - 3y.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the minimum value of f(x) = 5x^2/2 + α/x^5, x > 0 is 14, then the value of α is equal to -
A.sol_text: Given f(x) = 5x^2/2 + α/x^5 for x > 0. Taking derivative: f'(x) = 5x - 5α/x^6 = 0. Solving: x = (α)^(1/7). At this critical point, f(x)_min = 5(α)^(2/7)/2 + α/α^(5/7) = 14. Simplifying: 5α^(2/7)/2 + α^(2/7) = 14. This gives: 7α^(2/7)/2 = 14, so α^(2/7) = 4. Therefore α = 4^(7/2) = 128.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let α, β and γ be three positive real numbers. Let f(x) = αx^5 + βx^3 + γx, x ∈ R and g: R → R be such that g(f(x)) = x for all x ∈ R. If a₁, a₂, a₃, ..., aₙ be in arithmetic progression with mean zero, then the value of f(g((1/n)∑(i=1 to n)f(aᵢ))) is equal to
A.sol_text: Since a₁, a₂, a₃, ..., aₙ are in AP with mean zero: (a₁ + a₂ + a₃ + ... + aₙ)/n = 0. f(x) = αx^5 + βx^3 + γx is an odd function. ∑(i=1 to n)f(aᵢ) = α(a₁^5 + a₂^5 + ... + aₙ^5) + β(a₁^3 + a₂^3 + ... + aₙ^3) + γ(a₁ + a₂ + ... + aₙ) = 0 + 0 + 0 = 0 (since sum of odd powers of terms in AP with mean zero equals zero). Therefore (1/n)∑f(aᵢ) = 0. So f(g(0)) = f(g(f(0))) = f(0) = 0.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Consider the sequence a₁, a₂, a₃, ... such that a₁ = 1, a₂ = 2 and a_{n+2} = 2/a_{n+1} + a_n for n = 1, 2, 3, .... If ((a₁ + 1/a₂)/a₃) × ((a₂ + 1/a₃)/a₄) × ((a₃ + 1/a₄)/a₅) × ... × ((a₃₀ + 1/a₃₁)/a₃₂) = 2^α(⁶¹C₃₁), then α is equal to
A.sol_text: From the recurrence a_{n+2} = 2/a_{n+1} + a_n, we derive a_{n+2}a_{n+1} - a_n·a_{n+1} = 2, which gives a_{n+2}a_{n+1} = 2n + a₁a₂. Computing the telescoping product: ((a₁ + 1/a₂)/a₃) × ((a₂ + 1/a₃)/a₄) × ... × ((a₃₀ + 1/a₃₁)/a₃₂) = (3·5·7·...·61)/(4·6·8·...·62) = 2^{-60}(⁶¹C₃₁). Therefore α = -60.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The minimum value of the twice differentiable function f(x) = ∫[0 to x] e^(x-1) f'(t)dt - (x^2 - x + 1)e^x, x ∈ R, is
A.sol_text: Given f(x) = ∫[0 to x] e^(x-1) f'(t)dt - (x^2 - x + 1)e^x. Multiply both sides by e^(-x): e^(-x)f(x) = ∫[0 to x] e^(t-1)f'(t)dt - (x^2 - x + 1). Differentiate both sides: e^x f'(x) - f(x)e^(-x) = e^(x-1)f'(x) - 2x + 1, which gives f(x) = e^x(2x - 1). Then f'(x) = e^x(2x + 1) and f''(x) = e^x(2x + 3). Setting f'(x) = 0: 2x + 1 = 0, so x = -1/2. Since f''(-1/2) = e^(-1/2)(2(-1/2) + 3) = e^(-1/2)(2) > 0, this is a minimum. Minimum value = f(-1/2) = e^(-1/2)(2(-1/2) - 1) = e^(-1/2)(-2) = -2/sqrt(e).

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let S be the set of all passwords which are six to eight characters long, where each character is either an alphabet from {A, B, C, D, E} or a number from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}; with the repetition of characters allowed. If the number of passwords in S whose at least one character is a number from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} is alpha × 5^6, then alpha is equal to ______.
B.sol_text: For 6 character password: Total ways with at least one number = 10^6 - 5^6. For 7 character password: 10^7 - 5^7. For 8 character password: 10^8 - 5^8. Total number of passwords = (10^6 + 10^7 + 10^8) - (5^6 + 5^7 + 5^8) = 5^6(2^6 + 5×2^7 + 25×2^8 - 1 - 5 - 25) = 5^6(64 + 640 + 6400 - 31) = 5^6 × 7073. Therefore alpha = 7073.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let P(-2, -1, 1) and Q(56/17, 43/17, 111/17) be the vertices of the rhombus PRQS. If the direction ratios of the diagonal RS are α, -1, β, where both α and β are integers of minimum absolute values, then α^2 + β^2 is equal to
B.sol_text: Given P(-2, -1, 1) and Q(56/17, 43/17, 111/17) are vertices of rhombus PRQS. The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. Direction ratios of PQ are <90/17, 60/17, 94/17> or simplified <45, 30, 47>. For the diagonals to be perpendicular: α(45) + (-1)(30) + β(47) = 0, which gives 45α + 47β = 30. Solving for minimum integer values: α = (30 - 47β)/45. For β = 15, α = (30 - 705)/45 = -675/45 = -15. Therefore α^2 + β^2 = (-15)^2 + 15^2 = 225 + 225 = 450.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let f : [0, 1] → R be a twice differentiable function in (0, 1) such that f(0) = 3 and f(1) = 5. If the line y = 2x + 3 intersects the graph of f at only two distinct points in (0, 1) then the least number of points x ∈ (0, 1) at which f''(x) = 0, is _____.
B.sol_text: Let g(x) = f(x) - (2x + 3). Since the line y = 2x + 3 intersects the graph of f at only two distinct points in (0, 1), g(x) = 0 at exactly two points in (0, 1). Also g(0) = f(0) - 3 = 0 and g(1) = f(1) - 5 = 0. So g(x) has at least 3 zeros in [0, 1]: at x = 0, two interior points, and x = 1. By Rolle's theorem, g'(x) = 0 at least at 2 points in (0, 1). Since g'(x) = f'(x) - 2, we have f'(x) = 2 at least 2 points. By Rolle's theorem applied to g'(x), g''(x) = 0 at least once in (0, 1). Since g''(x) = f''(x), we have f''(x) = 0 at least once. To have the minimum, we need exactly 2 zeros of f''(x).
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.text: If ∫[0 to π/3] (15x^2)/((1+x^2)+sqrt(1+x^2)) dx = α√2 + β√3, where α, β are integers, then α + β is equal to
B.sol_text: Put x = tan(θ), dx = sec^2(θ)dθ. After substitution and simplification using sec^2(θ) - 1 = tan^2(θ), let 1 + sec(θ) = t^2. This gives sec(θ)tan(θ)dθ = 2tdt. The integral becomes 30∫[√2 to √3](t^4 - 2t^2)dt. Evaluating: 30[(t^5/5 - 2t^3/3)]|√2 to √3 = 30[(9√3/5 - 2√3) - (4√2/5 - 4√2/3)] = 16√2 - 6√3. Therefore α = 16, β = -6, so α + β = 10.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let A = [1 -1; 2 α] and B = [β 1; 1 0], α, β ∈ ℝ. Let α₁ be the value of α which satisfies (A + B)² = A² + [2 2; 2 2] and α₂ be the value of α which satisfies (A + B)² = B². Then |α₁ - α₂| is equal to ____.
B.sol_text: For condition (A + B)² = A² + [2 2; 2 2]: Expanding (A + B)² = A² + B² + AB + BA. This gives B² + AB + BA = [2 2; 2 2]. Computing AB, BA, B², and comparing matrix elements yields α = 1, β = 0, so α₁ = 1. For condition (A + B)² = B²: This simplifies to A² + AB + BA = 0. Computing A², AB, BA and comparing elements yields α = -1, β = 0, so α₂ = -1. Therefore |α₁ - α₂| = |1 - (-1)| = 2.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.
